questions.question_text: In juvenile diabetes, depression is an independent risk factor for ALL of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Prolactin elevation is not found. The other answers have been associated to varying degrees.

questions.question_text: Lithium levels above which point can affect multiple organs and be fatal?
questions.explanation: However, signs of lithium toxicity can also occur at normal serum levels.

questions.question_text: True or False: The number needed to treat is always a whole number, rounded off to an integer.
questions.explanation: This practice occurs by convention.

questions.question_text: In the biopsychosocial model of formulation, which of the following components belong in the biological realm?
questions.explanation: Refer to Table 4.2.6.2.

questions.question_text: According to Kolvin, which of the following is FALSE for childhood onset schizophrenia?

options.text: Children with this condition have poorer premorbid social functioning
Children with this condition have poorer premorbid language functioning
Transient autistic symptoms are commonly seen in toddler years

questions.explanation: Childhood onset schizophrenia is a severe and pervasive condition with a nonepisodic and unremitting course.

questions.question_text: ALL of the following are examples of commonly used language test batteries EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The Vineland is an example of a parent report questionnaire. This question's primary purpose is to make the reader aware of the variety of commonly used language test batteries that assess a child's communication abilities.

questions.question_text: Classic characteristics of language in verbal children with autism spectrum disorders include ALL of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: When children with autism spectrum disorders begin talking, aspects of language form, including phonology, syntax, and morphology are relatively spared. These children generally show skills in language form that are at or close to those of mental-age mates. The other answers reflect common characteristics of language in autism.

questions.question_text: The Edinburgh High Risk Study has focused on the identification of a range of characteristics that identify individuals who are at increased risk for the development of schizophrenia. These characteristics include:

options.text: Situational anxiety, depression, lower performance IQ scores, social withdrawal, schizotypal features, and isolated hallucinations
Chronic delusions, situational anxiety, isolated hallucinations, decreased verbal IQ, and social withdrawal
Isolated hallucinations, mania, lower performance IQ scores, social withdrawal, and schizotypal features
Situational anxiety, depression, isolated hallucinations, social withdrawal, schizotypal features, and lower verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) scores

correct_answer.text: Situational anxiety, depression, isolated hallucinations, social withdrawal, schizotypal features, and lower verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) scores

correct_answers.text: Situational anxiety, depression, isolated hallucinations, social withdrawal, schizotypal features, and lower verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) scores

questions.explanation: Such characteristics could help identify those individuals who would most likely benefit from selective preventive interventions.

questions.question_text: The most current consensus recommendations from experts in pediatric bipolar disorder suggest medication taper may be considered once remission has been maintained for:
True or False: Although often described as involuntary, research suggests that tics are not analogous to other involuntary movements, such as choreas or dystonias.
Which of these patients could be diagnosed with pica?

options.text: A normally developed adult who eats his own fingernails
A toddler who eats his own hair
A severely retarded adult who eats feces
A teenager with autism who eats raw potatoes

questions.explanation: The definition of pica is the persistent eating of nonnutritive substances for at least a month in a manner that such eating is inappropriate to the developmental level and is not part of culturally sanctioned practice, so all of the answer options could be included.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of hearing impairment in children under the age of 18 years in the United States?

options.text: It affects 5% of children in this age group
The most common form is the result of inner ear infection
Acquired hearing loss is responsible for 60% of permanent hearing impairment
Genetic defects are the most common cause of permanent sensorineural hearing loss

correct_answer.text: Genetic defects are the most common cause of permanent sensorineural hearing loss

correct_answers.text: Genetic defects are the most common cause of permanent sensorineural hearing loss

questions.explanation: Genetic defects are the most common causes of permanent sensorineural hearing loss followed by complications of severe prematurity and intrauterine and postnatal infection.

questions.question_text: Relaxation training for children typically involves ALL of the following techniques EXCEPT:

The most dramatic piece of legislation for children and families in recent years is the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 in which government effectively reduced public entitlements to cash benefits resulting in ALL of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: States are granted greater flexibility in the use of federal welfare funds
States are obliged to impose work requirements for those receiving federal assistance
States are obliged to impose a 5-year lifetime limit for federal assistance
States are obliged to provide a basic health care plan for children under the poverty line

correct_answer.text: States are obliged to provide a basic health care plan for children under the poverty line

correct_answers.text: States are obliged to provide a basic health care plan for children under the poverty line

questions.explanation: This act replaced Aid to Families with Dependent Children with Temporary Assistance to Needy Families.

questions.question_text: When a clinician interviews a child with severe visual impairment, and the child gazes in his or her direction, the clinician is more likely to ascribe which of the following to the child:
questions.explanation: A more favorable assessment of cognitive and social capacities occurs when the child uses gaze direction.

questions.question_text: True or False: A recent pharmacokinetic study of paroxetine showed that children metabolize this selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) more slowly than adults do.
questions.explanation: Despite the shorter half-life of paroxetine in children, the investigators of the study still recommended once-daily dosing of the medication.

questions.question_text: In a major study, Treatment for Adolescents with Depression Study, fluoxetine was found to be:

options.text: Less efficacious than both placebo and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)
As efficacious as both placebo and CBT
More efficacious than both placebo and CBT
Unapprovable for the treatment of depression in children and adolescents

correct_answer.text: More efficacious than both placebo and CBT

correct_answers.text: More efficacious than both placebo and CBT

questions.explanation: This answer was one of the notable findings of the Treatment for Adolescents with Depression Study.

questions.question_text: The Individual with Disabilities Education Act defines "emotional disturbance," previously known as "serious emotional disturbance," as:

options.text: An inability to learn that cannot be explained by intellectual, sensory, or health factors
A tendency to develop physical symptoms or fears associated with personal or school problems
Inappropriate types of mood or behavior under normal circumstances
An inability to build or maintain satisfactory interpersonal relationships with peers and teachers

questions.explanation: A general mood of unhappiness or depression is also included. One or more of the conditions should be present to a marked degree for a long time and adversely affect educational performance.

questions.question_text: Major changes in family, school, and neighborhoods, along with successes in preventive medicine, such as immunizations, accounted for the emergence of which field?
questions.explanation: The field of developmental behavioral pediatrics emerged as the needs of pediatric patients changed. It is intended to enhance the capacity of pediatricians to identify, manage, and when necessary, refer children with behavioral and developmental concerns.

questions.question_text: True or False: Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment of choice for catatonia if pharmacological management fails.
Preschool children often have fears and worries because:

options.text: There is little differentiation between fantasy and reality
They feel simultaneously powerful and helpless
They are preoccupied with the constancy of important people in their lives
Their capacity for imagination is increasing

questions.explanation: Preschool children depend on routine and ritual to soothe their worries and to make the world seem less scary. At the same time, their imaginations are growing, and scary thoughts are often much scarier than reality. Because preschoolers have a simultaneous sense of power and helplessness, with the concurrent difficulty in distinguishing between fantasy and reality, they often have the concern that by thinking a scary thought, the thought will come true.

questions.question_text: True or False: The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)-IV does not require evidence of conduct disorder prior to age 15 years for a diagnosis of antisocial personality disorder.
What is the treatment of night terrors?

options.text: Have the child sleep with the parents as needed

questions.explanation: The problem is transient and not serious. A benzodiazepine can be tried if a child is too embarrassed to sleep at a friend's house or becomes inhibited by usual daytime activities. If the problem persists into adolescence, a neurological evaluation is warranted to rule out sleep-related seizures.

questions.question_text: According to Freud, development in the school-aged child is characterized by:

options.text: An opportunity for society to correct the influence of the family
An attempt to master the basics of the industry of society, by building on academic abilities

questions.explanation: Freud described middle childhood as a period of latency, or sexual dormancy, although later theorists determined that school-aged children are not, actually, sexually 'dormant.' The superego develops before middle childhood, during the oedipal phase. Erikson's stage of industry versus inferiority also describes middle childhood.

questions.question_text: Meta-analysis is a research synthesis of a set of studies that uses what statistic to indicate the strength of relationship between a treatment (or other independent variable) and the dependent variables?
questions.explanation: There are many types of effect size indices, including d effect size, r, the odds ratio, risk ratio, and number needed to treat.

questions.question_text: Morphometric magnetic resonance imaging studies of subjects with trichotillomania support findings for decreased volumes in the:
True or False: The electroencephalogram pattern during rapid eye movement sleep is low voltage, fast, and resembles the electroencephalogram of wakefulness.
questions.explanation: Neuronal firing, neurotransmitter release and uptake, and metabolic rates also resemble patterns of waking.

questions.question_text: Anna Freud's classic, The Ego and the Mechanisms of Defense, enumerated several patterns of defense already in the analytic literature, including repression and reaction formation, but which of the following mechanisms of defense did she discover?
questions.explanation: She also discovered turning passive to active, denial, intellectualization, displacement, and altruistic surrender.

questions.question_text: What is the typical starting dose of paroxetine for children?
questions.explanation: The usual dosage range is 10 to 40 mg daily. Please note that paroxetine is not the preferred first line agent in children and adolescents, because it seems to have a higher rate for the emergence of suicidal thinking than other agents.

questions.question_text: At about 7 to 9 months, a shift of qualitative reorganization occurs in infants as they develop a sense of intersubjectivity, which consists of:

options.text: The understanding that even when others cannot be seen or heard, they still exist
The understanding that others can understand their thoughts, feelings, gestures, and sounds
The understanding that others can see the things from their perspective
The understanding that they are connected to, but not in complete union with, their caregivers

correct_answer.text: The understanding that others can understand their thoughts, feelings, gestures, and sounds

correct_answers.text: The understanding that others can understand their thoughts, feelings, gestures, and sounds

questions.explanation: This qualitative shift has profound impact on reciprocal communication and familial belonging.

questions.question_text: True or False: The first code of ethics of the American Medical Association was based upon Thomas Percival's Code of Medical Ethics.
questions.explanation: A historical fact that warrants mentioning.

questions.question_text: Placebo-controlled studies have shown the efficacy of which tricyclic antidepressant in children and adolescents with obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD)?
At higher doses, venlafaxine selectively inhibits which of the following neuronal functions?
questions.explanation: At lower doses (less than 150 mg daily), venlafaxine inhibits only serotonin reuptake.

questions.question_text: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is one of the most common childhood onset psychiatric disorders affecting approximately what percentage of children worldwide?
Two groups of subjects are initially free of disease. One group has experienced the exposure and the other group has not. What type of study is this?
questions.explanation: At times single cohorts are available, but the measurement of the exposure of each subject will allow the construction of two or several cohorts according to exposure levels.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.text: The negative outcome of abuse cannot be avoided
The Adoption and Safe Family Act of 1997 recommended that abused children who were removed from their homes be in permanent placement by the end of the first year
Parental substance abuse rarely affects the management of child maltreatment
Psychotropic medications are more often prescribed for children in social service care than those in the community
Most children and adults involved in maltreatment receive mental health services

correct_answer.text: Psychotropic medications are more often prescribed for children in social service care than those in the community

correct_answers.text: Psychotropic medications are more often prescribed for children in social service care than those in the community

questions.explanation: Children involved in the child protective service are two to three times more likely to be prescribed psychotropic medication than children in the community.

questions.question_text: Neuroanatomical structures that have been implicated in tic disorders include ALL of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Areas of the cortex, especially the motor strip have been implicated in connection with the corticostriatal thalamocortical track, which includes the basal ganglia as a way station.

questions.question_text: Maternal smoking during pregnancy is associated with later behavioral problems in the child. Which of the following is a confounding factor?
questions.explanation: Maternal antisocial behavior is associated with smoking during pregnancy and, quite separately, with risk of child behavioral problems. Thus, the association between prenatal maternal smoking and later child behavioral problems could be accounted for entirely by the confounding effects of maternal antisocial behavior.

questions.question_text: Case reports identify which of the following as a comorbid occurrence with gender identity disorder, one that might conceivably be linked by traits of behavioral rigidity and obsessionality?

options.text: Pervasive developmental disorder, not otherwise specified

correct_answer.text: Pervasive developmental disorder, not otherwise specified

correct_answers.text: Pervasive developmental disorder, not otherwise specified

questions.question_text: The DSM-III classified conduct disorder by dividing it into four subgroups according to whether children were socialized or undersocialized, and aggressive or nonaggressive, but how does DSM-IV classify conduct disorder?
questions.explanation: By childhood or adolescent type, depending on whether there were symptoms prior to the age of 10 years.

questions.question_text: True or False: The system-of-care model places the child and family at the center of the clinical process and as full partners at all levels of system planning.
questions.explanation: Family driven care is a cornerstone of the system-of-care approach.

questions.question_text: True or False: The course of borderline personality disorder (BPD) is highly stable with symptoms persistent.
questions.explanation: Findings are inconsistent, although, overall, the course of borderline personality disorder is considered less entrenched than it was historically.

questions.question_text: ALL of the following psychotropic medications have narrow therapeutic indices for clinical effectiveness, but significant adverse effects with toxicity EXCEPT:
True or False: A forensic evaluation affords the opportunity for therapeutic treatment for those clients who may not necessarily have access to psychiatric services.
questions.explanation: Forensic evaluations are only intended to help the court find the truth in a given situation and to address the legal question at hand. Whenever possible, forensic evaluations should be separated from treatment.

questions.question_text: A method of coping that uses strategies that avoid confronting pain, such as avoidance, denial, and wishful thinking is known as:
questions.explanation: Accommodative coping—accepting and adjusting to pain by regulating attention and thought patterns—is associated with lower levels of pain, somatic complaints, and emotional distress for those with chronic pain. Passive coping is associated with more distress.

questions.question_text: The President's New Freedom Commission on Mental Health Report (2003) presented six major goals for a transformed mental health system, including which of the following:

options.text: Increasing Americans' understanding of mental health's limited impact on overall health
Screening of high school students' mental health
Privatization of Medicaid mental health services
Reduction of the intrusion of technology to access mental health care
Elimination of disparities in mental health care

correct_answer.text: Elimination of disparities in mental health care

correct_answers.text: Elimination of disparities in mental health care

questions.question_text: In studies of 3-year olds and preschool aggression, what percentage displays little or no aggression?
questions.explanation: This question is meant to highlight how normative physical aggression among 3-year olds is, but that this behavior diminishes upon school entry and through the elementary school years.

questions.question_text: Epidemiological studies suggest the percentage of children suffering 'extreme functional impairments' from psychiatric disorders is in what range?
questions.explanation: Moreover, up to 10% to 20% have diagnosable disorders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the psychoanalytic concept of resistance in the therapeutic process is FALSE? It is a defense against:
True or False: IQ scores are predictive of academic abilities in school-aged children.
The DSM-IV includes ALL of the following categories EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) classifies types of learning disorders by referencing the primary academic areas of difficulty. The classification includes reading disorder, mathematics disorder, disorder of written expression, and learning disorder not otherwise specified.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the statistic of choice to describe the center of a distribution if data are normally distributed?
True or False: IQ is stable from infancy.
questions.explanation: Although this belief was well rooted during the earlier decades of the 20th century, it has been discredited and infant intelligence quotient (IQ) tests are presently not used.

questions.question_text: Approximately what fraction of individuals with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) experience one or more comorbid lifetime diagnoses?
Which of the following is true of the genetics of homosexuality?

options.text: Monozygotic male twins have concordance rates between 22% and 30%
Dizygotic male twins have concordance rates between 52% and 66%
Monozygotic female twins have concordance rates of 48%
Dizygotic female twins have concordance rates of 48%

correct_answer.text: Monozygotic female twins have concordance rates of 48%

correct_answers.text: Monozygotic female twins have concordance rates of 48%

questions.explanation: Several studies have shown monozygotic male twins to have concordance rates between 52% and 66% and female twins 48%. For dizygotic male twins the concordance rates have been shown to be 22% to 30% and for female twins it is 16%.

questions.question_text: Compared to healthy controls, the rates of psychological disorders in children with chronic medical illness are:

options.text: Two to four times the rate of children without a chronic medical illness
Four to six times the rate of children without a chronic medical illness
Lower than children without a chronic medical illness
The same as children without a chronic medical illness

correct_answer.text: Two to four times the rate of children without a chronic medical illness

correct_answers.text: Two to four times the rate of children without a chronic medical illness

questions.explanation: It varies by chronic medical illness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the normal milestone for a child's ability to eat solid food?
Psychometric tests are based on their reliability and validity. What is the least acceptable score of the reliability coefficient generally recommended for diagnostic tests?
questions.explanation: For screening tests, the reliability coefficient should be at least 0.80.

questions.question_text: Typically, impairment resulting from psychopathology is assessed in four domains and includes each of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Ability to enjoy and obtain satisfaction from life

questions.explanation: The importance of including impairment in case definition has been well presented, because the prevalence of psychiatric disorders on the basis of symptoms alone reaches 50% but is under 20% if impairment is included in case definition.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about serving snacks in a group is FALSE?

options.text: The food should be voted on by the group, with the leaders retaining veto power
Promotes more intimate, relaxed interactions that often help task accomplishment
Dietary restrictions should be accommodated by the entire group whenever possible
It is a nurturing, tangible support
Protests about the snack selection should be understood as part of the group attempting to establish and maintain its trust in the group leadership

correct_answer.text: The food should be voted on by the group, with the leaders retaining veto power

correct_answers.text: The food should be voted on by the group, with the leaders retaining veto power

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is NOT a DSM-IV criterion for Asperger's disorder?

options.text: Restricted, repetitive and stereotyped patterns of behavior, interests, and activities
Clinically significant general delay in language
Does not meet criteria for another specific pervasive developmental disorder
Lack of clinically significant cognitive delay

correct_answer.text: Clinically significant general delay in language

correct_answers.text: Clinically significant general delay in language

questions.question_text: Studies by Hetherington and colleagues found that the long-term effects of divorce and remarriage appear to be related to a number of factors including ALL of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: The degree of amicability in the divorce proceedings

correct_answer.text: The degree of amicability in the divorce proceedings

correct_answers.text: The degree of amicability in the divorce proceedings

questions.explanation: The quality of the home environment also plays a factor, but the amicability of the divorce is not specifically included in the study's findings.

questions.question_text: The world's first statute regarding adoption was passed in:
True or False: A personality disorder cannot be diagnosed in a child.
questions.explanation: However, the pattern of a personality disorder should be stable and of long duration. This criterion, along with the fluid developmental processes of children, makes the diagnosis difficult.

questions.question_text: The proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy study conducted by Thomas and colleagues in children with schizophrenia showed which one of the following?

options.text: The ratio of NAA to creatine was equivocal in the occipital lobes of children with schizophrenia
The ratio of NAA to creatine was significantly lower in the occipital lobes of children with schizophrenia
The ratio of NAA to creatine was significantly higher in the occipital lobes of children with schizophrenia
The ratio of NAA to creatine was significantly lower in the parietal lobes of children with schizophrenia
The ratio of N-acetylaspartate (NAA) to creatine was significantly lower in the frontal lobes of children with schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: The ratio of N-acetylaspartate (NAA) to creatine was significantly lower in the frontal lobes of children with schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: The ratio of N-acetylaspartate (NAA) to creatine was significantly lower in the frontal lobes of children with schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Thomas and colleagues conducted a proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy study of children with schizophrenia and healthy children in which they found that the ratio of N-acetylaspartate to creatine was significantly lower in the frontal lobes of children with schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Besides psychosocial dwarfism, other disorders involving short stature include ALL of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Other disorders involving short stature include primary dwarfism, intrauterine growth retardation with persistent small size, hypopituitarism from a variety of etiologies, Turner's syndrome (XO chromosomal pattern), osteochondrodystrophies, constitutionally delayed growth, and growth stunting secondary to chronic malnutrition with or without chronic disease.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following are risk factors for Stevens–Johnson syndrome while on lamotrigine therapy?
questions.explanation: These risk factors are especially true for children.

questions.question_text: In resilience research, what is the conceptual definition of vulnerability factors?

options.text: The factors that exacerbate the negative effects of the risk condition
The factors that indicate the inherent weaknesses in the individual
The factors that hinder positive adaptation in spite of the risk condition
The factors that propagate or produce the risk condition

correct_answer.text: The factors that exacerbate the negative effects of the risk condition

correct_answers.text: The factors that exacerbate the negative effects of the risk condition

questions.explanation: Vulnerability and protective factors modify the negative effects of adverse life events; the former factor worsens those effects.

questions.question_text: True or False: The proportion of adolescents in poor and near-poor families without insurance decreased between 1995 and 2002.
True or False: Less than half of the National Institute of Mental Health funded intervention proposals and programs include a family component.
questions.explanation: As parent involvement has been shown to enhance engagement in treatment, retention, and treatment outcome, the National Institute of Mental Health has encouraged the use of family interventions in investigative projects; more than half of National Institute of Mental Health funded intervention proposals and programs include a family component.

questions.question_text: In the field of infant assessments, one of the most commonly used instruments following the Piagetian model is the Infant Psychological Development Scale, which assesses an infant's ability to perform ALL of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The Brazelton Neonatal Behavioral Assessment Scale assesses social responsiveness.

questions.question_text: In the treatment of ADHD with atomoxetine, doses above which amount are not likely to produce additional benefit?
questions.explanation: The total daily dose of atomoxetine usually falls between 0.8 and 1.2 mg/kg.

questions.question_text: Higher rates of suicide are found in both children and adults with epilepsy. Which epilepsy in adults accounts for the highest rate?
questions.explanation: In one retrospective chart review of children with suicide attempts, those with epilepsy had a rate 15 times that of the general population.

questions.question_text: True or False: Children with less language ability may exhibit greater levels of physical aggression than their more verbal peers.
questions.explanation: Children with fewer words may have no other means to express their needs and frustrations.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following organizations were formed specifically for the mission of education and training?

options.text: American Association of Directors of Psychiatric Residency Training
American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
American Association of Psychiatric Clinics for Children

questions.explanation: The American Association of Psychiatric Clinics for Children was formed in 1946 but not solely for education and training.

questions.question_text: A study by Richard Green of 66 feminine boys and 56 control boys examined sexual orientation in fantasy and behavior, initially at 7 years of age and again at 19 years of age. Which statement(s) capture(s) the findings?

options.text: Of those available at follow up, only one youth at the age of 18 years was gender dysphoric to the extent of considering sex reassignment surgery
0% to 4% of the control boys were bisexual or homosexual
75% to 80% of the previously feminine boys were bisexual or homosexual at follow up

questions.explanation: Note that gender identity disorder was not assessed in this study.

questions.question_text: What are the most common compulsions in adolescents?
questions.explanation: The answer options are listed in descending order of frequency from A to D.

questions.question_text: Hermine von Hug-Hellmuth was credited as the first to undertake psychoanalytic therapy of children and adolescents. What was the most significant observation she made regarding the therapy and the expression of unconscious conflict in children as compared with adults?

options.text: That spontaneous play could stand in the place of verbal communications
That regression was a common component of the therapy
That free association unfolds in similar ways
That children require therapeutic aids in expression of unconscious conflict
That a working alliance with parents was essential for child improvement

correct_answer.text: That spontaneous play could stand in the place of verbal communications

correct_answers.text: That spontaneous play could stand in the place of verbal communications

questions.explanation: Furthermore, von Hug-Hellmuth observed that fully conscious analytic understanding of unconscious conflicts was not a prerequisite for therapeutic effect in children.

questions.question_text: True or False: In interviewing adolescents, clinicians can decrease resistance by beginning the history taking by inquiring first about the adolescent's interests, strengths, and musical preferences.
questions.explanation: This is an important clinical point worth knowing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following types of therapy groups requires substantial cognitive growth and ability in its members, especially regarding emotionally charged topics?
True or False: When genes are expressed, for example, as in the transcription of growth hormone, they are expressed in all cell lineages that have the gene.
questions.explanation: Genes remain quiescent in some cell lineages or are repressed after a period of activity.

questions.question_text: Which professional organization established in 1924 attempted to unify the disciplines of psychiatric diagnosis and child treatment by bringing together psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers, and the judiciary interested in child guidance?

options.text: American Association of Psychiatric Clinics for Children
American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology
American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry

questions.explanation: The American Association of Psychiatric Clinics for Children grew out of the American Orthopsychiatric Association and was established in 1945.

questions.question_text: Angelman and Prader-Willi syndromes, disorders of genomic imprinting, share ALL of the following features EXCEPT:

options.text: Both disorders are caused by a deletion on chromosome 15 or by receiving two copies of chromosome 15 from one parent
Individuals with both disorders are hypotonic as infants
Both are rare disorders with a prevalence of 1 in 10,000 births
Both are the result of deletions from maternally derived chromosomes
Individuals with both disorders have some degree of mental retardation (MR)

correct_answer.text: Both are the result of deletions from maternally derived chromosomes

correct_answers.text: Both are the result of deletions from maternally derived chromosomes

questions.explanation: The deletion on chromosome 15 (15q11-15q13) derives from the father in most cases of Prader-Willi syndrome and from the mother in most individuals with Angelman syndrome.

questions.question_text: True or False: A psychoanalytic finding indicates that parental harshness appears to weaken the superego functions of the child.
questions.explanation: When a parent inflicts punishment that hurts the child, the child's focus is promoted on the external struggle with the parent.

questions.question_text: Symptoms frequently reported in children with conversion disorder include ALL of the following EXCEPT:
The possibility of which adverse event cautions against the abrupt discontinuation of clonidine?
A living donor transplant is possible for which organs?
questions.explanation: Living donors may be biologically related, emotionally connected but not related, or unrelated and anonymous.

questions.question_text: For the treatment of anorexia nervosa, the following form of psychotherapy has been proven most effective:

options.text: No specific psychotherapy approach has proven most effective

correct_answer.text: No specific psychotherapy approach has proven most effective

correct_answers.text: No specific psychotherapy approach has proven most effective

questions.explanation: The Cochrane review of six small outpatient psychotherapy trials concluded that no specific psychotherapy approach can be recommended.

questions.question_text: During the middle phase of IPT for depressed adolescents, the therapist teaches the adolescent-specific strategies that can help with interpersonal difficulties. One strategy is to facilitate discussion of painful feelings and to help the adolescent use emotional experiences to better understand the link between mood and relationships. What is this technique called?
Why should the long-term use (greater than a month) of anticholinergic medications be avoided if possible in children?

options.text: The risk of an acute dystonic reaction

questions.explanation: Anticholinergic medications decrease secretions, which can cause a Sjogren-like iatrogenic syndrome, which can lead to widespread cavities.

questions.question_text: Approximately how many children are forced into prostitution worldwide each year?
questions.explanation: Approximately 1 million children are forced into prostitution worldwide each year.

questions.question_text: A therapeutic dose of a benzodiazepine can be detected in the urine for how long?

Which is the type of neuronal receptor at which a neurotransmitter binds to a receptor protein, resulting in a change in the permeability of the associated ion channel in milliseconds, and the influx of ions such as Ca2+, Na+, K+, or Cl–?
questions.explanation: These are also called class I receptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications can increase serum lithium levels?
questions.explanation: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and tetracyclines can decrease urinary clearance of lithium.

questions.question_text: Child abuse and neglect are MOST LIKELY associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Child abuse can and does occur across all socioeconomic classes, but is most prevalent among the poor.

questions.question_text: True or False: For all tricyclic antidepressants, vital signs and electrocardiograms should be obtained when the maintenance dose has been achieved.
questions.explanation: Vital signs and electrocardiograms should be obtained prior to treatment and after dose adjustments.

questions.question_text: True or False: Persons with Asperger's disorder tend to have better verbal IQ than performance IQ, and persons with classic autistic disorder tend to have better performance IQ than verbal IQ.
Stierlin proposed which of following concepts to describe ways in which families negotiate a pathological separation to overcome fear of prolonged fusion?

options.text: Prescribing the symptom, exceptional solution, and paradoxical intervention

questions.question_text: What is a potentially fatal complication from chronic ipecac abuse?
questions.explanation: Cardiac failure may be caused by cardiomyopathy from ipecac abuse.

questions.question_text: Which antipsychotic is unlikely to produce neurological side effects even at high doses?
questions.explanation: Due to quetiapine's relatively low affinity for D2 receptors, it does not show the dose threshold effect resulting in neurological side effects observed with risperidone, olanzapine, and the first-generation agents.

questions.question_text: Insecure attachment behaviors include ALL of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Monitoring and seeking proximity to the parent

correct_answer.text: Monitoring and seeking proximity to the parent

questions.question_text: Over the last decade, which of the following has seen increased use by adolescents?
What is a side effect with desmopressin acetate?
questions.explanation: Hyponatremic seizures have been reported with intranasal desmopressin acetate.

questions.question_text: Gender identity is primarily determined through which of the following?
questions.explanation: Studies of infants with ambiguous genitalia established that gender identity is primarily determined through socialization.
